Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. ## What this changes This PR moves bundled session reads into existing database workers and carries committed facts through runtime authorization. **Example:** The Gateway reads session metadata for agent:main:main. - **Before:** Bundled callers can query SQLite synchronously on the Gateway thread. - **After:** Callers await worker reads and consume retained facts updated by committed writes. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Useful architectural work remains unready because the deferred disclosure guard and voice cleanup are incomplete. | | **Proof confidence** | 🧂 unranked krab **(1/6)** | Real behavior proof is necessary before merge. See [Before merge](#before-merge). | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Security review found an item that needs attention. | ## Product **Kind:** Refactor · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Synchronous session database reads can block Gateway work across routing, execution, plugins, and status rendering. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction implements the documented worker ownership model and preserves released synchronous SDK adapters. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep open: this maintainer-directed worker cutover has clear value, but both previously reported defects remain in the reviewed head. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `fad6192d21ded59a7c46b2b5ba4fe837284f8f12` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Authority-chain proof required: provide redacted terminal output or logs showing successful same-account CLI argv recovery and rejection before private argument transfer when history authority changes during broker or relay transport preparation. The earlier isolated Gateway workload supports ordinary worker behavior, while the inspected mocked relay regression covers stdin only. Redact credentials, IPs, phone numbers, and non-public endpoints. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Validate history at the deferred argv disclosure boundary (P1)** - For a CLI backend carrying recovered history in argv, prepareSpawn validates history before createChildAdapter constructs the transport. The relay then awaits transportReady before sending the start frame containing those arguments. If history ownership or coverage changes during that wait, the later assertCurrent checks only run liveness because executePreparedCliRun now installs cliHistoryWriter.assertCurrent instead of assertReadable. The private prompt can therefore cross the process boundary after its history authority has been revoked. Perform history validation after deferred transport preparation and preserve its authority through the actual argument transfer. This previously reported blocker remains unchanged. - [ ] **Release voice-request authorization when the request settles (P2)** - When talk.voice.get or talk.voice.set requires session facts, resolveSessionMutationAuthorizationAsync allocates retained sharing reads and session-change subscriptions. resolveVoiceCaller returns only closures using authorization.assertCurrent, so neither successful requests nor subsequent handler failures release this newly allocated authorization. Repeated voice requests accumulate retained readers and listeners, increasing memory and publication work. Return the release operation with the caller and invoke it from the handlers' finally blocks, including resolution failures after acquisition. The body records this as a follow-up, but the defect remains in this head. - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Run liveness does not establish history ownership** - The original history contract independently binds transcript coverage and the selected account; keeping the run active cannot substitute for that authorization. - [ ] **Explain or restore the original intent of CLI history disclosure** - e20b56c0b26eec6db2af373da4598c8f40bee626: Recover saved CLI context without crossing authentication-account boundaries, including during deferred execution. ## Findings - [P1] Validate history at the deferred argv disclosure boundary — `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts:354-356` - [P2] Release voice-request authorization when the request settles — `src/gateway/talk/handlers/voice.ts:41-47` - [high] Run liveness does not establish history ownership — `src/agents/cli-runner/execute.ts:131` ### Provenance - `CLI history disclosure` changes intended behavior without addressing why it exists (e20b56c0b26eec6db2af373da4598c8f40bee626: Recover saved CLI context without crossing authentication-account boundaries, including during deferred execution.) ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied evidence does not show allowed same-account argv recovery and rejection before argument transfer when history authority changes during broker or relay preparation; base-failing regression execution for that scenario is also unshown.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Gateway routing, agent execution, plugins, and status rendering consume session metadata; database workers return prepared facts, while runtime owners authorize subsequent effects. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Gateway and bundled callers] --> B[Session read preparation] B --> C[Database workers] C --> D[Prepared session facts] E[Committed write receipts] --> D D --> F[Live authority checks] F --> G[Execution and disclosure] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Complete the worker cutover while preserving history authorization at argument disclosure and releasing request-owned voice facts. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source tracing establishes both remaining paths; no target code was executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Using existing workers and committed receipts fits the repository architecture, provided final-effect authorization and ownership cleanup remain intact. Full review comments: - [P1] Validate history at the deferred argv disclosure boundary — `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts:354-356` For a CLI backend carrying recovered history in argv, prepareSpawn validates history before createChildAdapter constructs the transport. The relay then awaits transportReady before sending the start frame containing those arguments. If history ownership or coverage changes during that wait, the later assertCurrent checks only run liveness because executePreparedCliRun now installs cliHistoryWriter.assertCurrent instead of assertReadable. The private prompt can therefore cross the process boundary after its history authority has been revoked. Perform history validation after deferred transport preparation and preserve its authority through the actual argument transfer. This previously reported blocker remains unchanged. Confidence: 0.98 - [P2] Release voice-request authorization when the request settles — `src/gateway/talk/handlers/voice.ts:41-47` When talk.voice.get or talk.voice.set requires session facts, resolveSessionMutationAuthorizationAsync allocates retained sharing reads and session-change subscriptions. resolveVoiceCaller returns only closures using authorization.assertCurrent, so neither successful requests nor subsequent handler failures release this newly allocated authorization. Repeated voice requests accumulate retained readers and listeners, increasing memory and publication work. Return the release operation with the caller and invoke it from the handlers' finally blocks, including resolution failures after acquisition.
